newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian shares end little changed, sluggish trade.
newsitem.headline: Indian shares end little changed, sluggish trade.

text.p: ** (1300 GMT) Indian stocks finish mixed, rangebound trade
** Major players keep to the sidelines, dull outlook
** HDFC, SKF Bearings advance after both firms post rise
in first half 1996/97 profits
** Benchmark Bombay Stock Exchange 30-share index loses
14.29 points or 0.46 percent to 3,104.66
** NSE index down 0.56 pct, Calcutta index falls 0.45 pct
** Madras index rises 0.23 percent
Indian shares ended little changed in lethargic trade on Wednesday with most participants sitting out on the sidelines, traders said.
"The market continues to be range-bound," said Purvesh Shah, dealer at Bombay-based brokerage Asit C Mehta. He said lack of market-moving news kept the market in a narrow range.
The benchmark 30-share index of the Bombay Stock Exchange (BSE) closed 14.29 points or 0.46 percent lower at 3,104.66.
Analysts said the market would take cue from six-month 1996/97 results (April-March) of Reliance due on Friday.
They expect the country's top private sector firm to report sharply lower profits for the first half due to higher costs, lower product prices and flat volume growth.
"The profits are going to be sharply down," said Jal Irani, petrochemicals analyst at Jardine Fleming India Broking.
Reliance ended 0.25 rupees lower at 188.75 on the BSE.
Traders said the market was pinning hopes on the Reserve Bank of India's monetary policy for the second half of 1996/97 (April-March) due on Saturday.
The central bank is expected to ease liquidity conditions and put pressure on high interest rates, analysts said.

HDFC and SKF Bearings advanced after both firms posted a rise in their six-month 1996/97 (April-March) net profits on Tuesday. SKF Bearings gained 150 rupees or 6.12 percent to 2,600. HDFC rose 52.50 rupees or 2.41 percent to 2,227.75.
The 50-stock National Stock Exchange index lost 5.0 points or 0.56 percent to 892.77 and the Calcutta exchange index 1.90 points to 416.63. The Delhi index fell 1.96 to 706.01.
But the Madras index was up 7.37 points to 3,195.78
--ANSHUMAN DAGA, Bombay newsroom +91-22-265 9000
